title: Arakelov geometry and heights of abelian varieties, Part II: adelic bigness on curve families
summary: Part II of ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights, starting where it stops (hermitian degree, ĈH¹ and heights of points). It plans the projective model theory of arithmetic intersection numbers, metrized Deligne pairings and arithmetic volumes; Yuan–Zhang adelic line bundles on quasi-projective schemes over ℤ or a field with their analytification, intersection theory, volumes, heights, height inequality, equidistribution and invariant extensions; Moriwaki heights; Zhang's admissible metrics on curves and Yuan's canonical admissible bundles on curve families; the global ε, φ and Noether divisors; Yuan's theorem that the admissible canonical bundle is nef and big under maximal variation; potential bigness; and the uniform comparison of Zhang's admissible self-intersection with the stable Faltings height.
readme:
# Arakelov geometry and heights of abelian varieties, Part II: adelic bigness on curve families

This roadmap is the Part II of ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights (TauCetiRoadmap pull request #1000). That roadmap builds the hermitian degree over rings of integers, arithmetic divisors with smooth Green functions and ĈH¹ on regular arithmetic schemes, heights of algebraic points for metrized line bundles, the Faltings metric and the relative and stable Faltings heights; it explicitly leaves out higher arithmetic intersection products and general adelic intersection theory. This roadmap starts there. Its end points are the two theorems of Xinyi Yuan's "Arithmetic bigness and a uniform Bogomolov-type result" (Annals 203, 2026) that concern the admissible canonical bundle itself:

1. **Bigness.** For a smooth family π : X → S of curves of genus g > 1 with maximal variation over a flat quasi-projective normal integral scheme S over ℤ or a field, Yuan's canonical admissible adelic line bundle ω\_{X/S,a} is nef and big on X, and π\_\*⟨ω\_a, ω\_a⟩ is nef and big on S (Theorems 1.3, 3.1, 3.2; AH.11). Together with the theta identities it gives potential bigness of the theta pullbacks along the Abel, difference and universal-shift maps (Theorems 4.1, 4.5; AH.12).

2. **Uniform comparison.** There are c₃(g), c₄(g) > 0 with c₃·max{h\_Fal(C), 1} ≤ [ω²\_{C/K,a}] ≤ c₄·max{h\_Fal(C), 1} for every curve of genus g over every number field and (non-isotrivial) over every one-variable function field (Theorem 1.4; AH.13).

To get there the roadmap plans the theory those theorems are written in: the projective model case of arithmetic intersection theory (AH.0), Yuan–Zhang's adelic divisors and adelic line bundles on quasi-projective schemes with their analytification, intersection theory, Deligne pairing, volumes, heights, height inequality, fundamental inequality, equidistribution and invariant extensions (AH.1–AH.5), Moriwaki's heights over finitely generated fields (AH.6), Zhang's admissible metrics on curves (AH.7) and their family version (AH.8), the theta identities (AH.9) and the global ε, φ and Noether divisors (AH.10). The uniform Bogomolov theorem itself (Yuan Theorem 1.1) and the small-points bounds are the work of HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructionsPartII, which imports AH.4, AH.5, AH.8, AH.12 and AH.13.

## Reading the plan

Each layer states its targets and then its nodes, numbered §k.i. Definitions and constructions carry an API outline and unit tests that a plausible wrong definition fails; theorems carry hypotheses, a proof route, acceptance checks and prerequisites. Every node cites where its sources state or prove it, in our own words, with theorem and page numbers. The plan is at target level (PROTOCOL.md §2): smaller steps stay in the proof routes. Node identifiers are relative to this roadmap; prerequisites in other roadmaps keep their full identifiers. Every node is a plan, not a formalization.

## Conventions

- k is ℤ (the arithmetic case) or a field (the geometric case). A projective arithmetic variety is an integral scheme projective and flat over ℤ; "quasi-projective arithmetic variety" likewise. All adelic objects are over the base k, written P̂ic(X/k).
- Green functions use −log‖s‖, so d̂iv(f) = (div f, −log\|f\|) and c₁(L̄) = (1/πi)∂∂̄log‖s‖ + δ\_div(s) (Yuan–Zhang §2.1). The parent roadmap uses −log‖s‖² (Gillet–Soulé); the comparison doubles Green functions (§0.1).
- Heights over a number field K are absolute: h\_L̄(x) = deĝ(L̄\|\_x)/[K(x) : ℚ], with archimedean places weighted 1 (real) or 2 (complex). Over a one-variable function field K/k the normalization is by residue degrees over the fixed k: ‖·‖\_v = e^{−[k(v):k] ord\_v}, and h = deĝ/[K(x) : K].
- The Faltings metric is ‖α‖² = (i^{g²}/2^g)∫α∧ᾱ (Faltings' normalization, as in Yuan §4.3.1 and the parent's §2.1); Deligne's and Yuan–Zhang's is (2π)^{−g}\|∫α∧ᾱ\|, and h\_Del = h\_Fal + (g/2)log π (parent §2.7). h\_Fal always denotes the stable height.
- Curves: a smooth relative curve is smooth projective with geometrically connected fibres. Every target from AH.7 on assumes genus g > 1; Yuan states several results for g > 0, but the genus-one normalization is not proved (PAPER-YUAN-26/E8, E28). Maximal variation means the moduli map S → M\_{g,k} is generically finite (StableReductionPartII MC.6/maximal-variation); over a function field K/k it is taken over the constant field k (PAPER-YUAN-26/E1).
- w = ω̄\_{X/S,a}, D = Ō(Δ)\_a, P = π\_\*⟨w, w⟩, ⟨A, B⟩ = π\_\*⟨A, B⟩, and Θ̄ is the canonical [2]-invariant extension of the symmetric rigidified twice-theta bundle Θ = Δ\_J^\*P^∨ on J = Pic⁰\_{X/S}. ĥ = ½ĥ\_Θ is the Néron–Tate height of the symmetric theta class.
- Graph invariants (ε, φ, τ, δ, δᵢ) are Zhang's, for unit edge lengths on the minimal regular model and \|ϖ\| = e^{−1}; under a finite extension they scale by the ramification index (PAPER-YUAN-26/E3).

stages.title: Projective arithmetic intersection theory: the model case
stages.description:
**Targets.** Hermitian line bundles with continuous, semipositive and integrable metrics on projective arithmetic varieties, their Monge–Ampère measures, arithmetic intersection numbers by the inductive formula, the metrized Deligne pairing along projective flat morphisms, and arithmetic volumes with the Hilbert–Samuel formula and the Siu inequality. These are the model inputs that every limit construction of the later layers reduces to; the geometric analogue over a field is the ordinary intersection theory of SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.5.

**Sources.** Yuan–Zhang §2.1, §§4.2–4.4, §5.2; Yuan 2008 §2.

stages.title: Adelic divisors and adelic line bundles
stages.description:
**Targets.** Yuan–Zhang adelic divisors and adelic line bundles on flat quasi-projective integral schemes over k = ℤ or a field: model adelic divisors of mixed coefficients, the boundary norm and its completion, the groupoid P̂ic(U/k) of adelic line bundles, the divisor presentation, effectivity, strong nefness, nefness and integrability, pullbacks, limits to essentially quasi-projective schemes (global fields, finitely generated fields), the archimedean base (ℂ, |·|), and the comparison with the compactified Picard group of an arithmetic curve.

**Sources.** Yuan–Zhang §§2.2–2.7; Yuan §2.1 pp. 18–21, 23–25.

stages.title: Berkovich analytification and metrized line bundles
stages.description:
**Targets.** The global Berkovich analytification (U/k)^an over the Banach ring ℤ (or a trivially valued field), analytic arithmetic divisors and continuous metrized line bundles on it, injectivity and full faithfulness of analytification of adelic objects, density of divisorial points, effectivity tested on Green functions, canonical measures on fibres, and canonical metrics over trivially valued fields.

**Sources.** Yuan–Zhang Chapter 3, Lemma 5.1.2; Yuan §2.1 pp. 21–22, §3.2 p. 47, §A.6 p. 119.

stages.title: Intersection numbers and the adelic Deligne pairing
stages.description:
**Targets.** The absolute intersection pairing of integrable adelic line bundles, the relative Deligne pairing along projective flat morphisms with normal base, its composition and projection formulas, and injectivity of pullback along fibrations with geometrically connected fibres with descent of fibrewise constant metrics.

**Sources.** Yuan–Zhang §§4.1, 4.5, 4.6; Yuan Lemmas 2.1–2.2 pp. 25–27.

stages.title: Effective sections, volumes and heights
stages.description:
**Targets.** Effective sections and ĥ⁰ of adelic line bundles, the adelic volume and bigness, the adelic Hilbert–Samuel formula and Siu inequality, positivity of Deligne pairings of nef and big bundles, invariance of nef bigness under finite covers, volumes over global fields, domination by nef effective model divisors, heights of algebraic points and vector-valued heights over finitely generated fields, the height inequality and the fundamental inequality.

**Sources.** Yuan–Zhang §§5.1–5.3; Yuan §2.1 pp. 22–25, §4.1.2 pp. 63–65, Remark 4.4 p. 67.

stages.title: Equidistribution, invariant extensions and the adelic Hodge bundle
stages.description:
**Targets.** Equidistribution of generic small sequences for nef adelic line bundles on quasi-projective varieties, invariant adelic extensions for polarized dynamical systems over a base (the Tate limit), non-degenerate subvarieties with their height inequality and equidistribution, and the adelic Hodge bundle of a family of curves with the determinant L² metric.

**Sources.** Yuan–Zhang §§5.4, 5.5, 6.1, 6.2; Yuan §3.1.3 pp. 43–44; DeMarco–Mavraki–Ye §4.

stages.title: Moriwaki heights over finitely generated fields
stages.description:
**Targets.** Moriwaki polarizations of a finitely generated field over ℚ, the Moriwaki height as a Yuan–Zhang height and its height machine, the Moriwaki Néron–Tate height, and the Silverman–Tate and specialization theorems with Moriwaki heights.

**Sources.** Moriwaki 2000 §3; Gao–Habegger Appendix A; Yuan–Zhang §5.3.

stages.title: Local admissible metrics on curves
stages.description:
**Targets.** For a smooth projective geometrically integral curve C of genus g > 0 over a complete non-archimedean field: Tate's admissible metrics on abelian varieties, admissibility on C through the Jacobian and on C², the canonical admissible measure, Zhang's canonical pair of admissible metrics on ω_C and O(Δ), the explicit graph formulas at split semistable reduction, rescaling, good reduction and trivially valued fields, and the global admissible bundles ω_{C/K,a} and O(Δ)_a over a global field. The archimedean theory is GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights GZ.2; graph measures and Green functions are TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic TB.3/TB.6.

**Sources.** Yuan Appendix A, pp. 101–119; Zhang 1993 as reproved there.

stages.title: Admissible adelic bundles on curve families
stages.description:
**Targets.** For a smooth projective family π : X → S of geometrically connected curves of genus g > 1 over a flat quasi-projective normal integral k-scheme: admissible adelic extensions on X, X ×_S X and abelian schemes over S, their existence and uniqueness modulo base metrics, the canonical admissible bundles ω_{X/S,a} and O(Δ)_a (Theorem 2.3), the canonical twice-theta bundle Θ̄ of the relative Jacobian, section divisors and evaluation, and the relative arithmetic Hodge index identity.

**Sources.** Yuan §§2.2–2.3, pp. 28–35; Yuan–Zhang Theorem 6.5.1.

stages.title: Theta identities and nefness of the admissible canonical bundle
stages.description:
**Targets.** The pullback formulas of Θ̄ along the Abel map i_α, the canonical map i_ω, the difference map j and the universal shift τ, with their Deligne self-pairings, and the resulting expression of ω_{X/S,a} as a positive combination of nef bundles: ω_{X/S,a} and ⟨ω_a, ω_a⟩ are nef.

**Sources.** Yuan Theorems 2.9–2.10, pp. 35–38.

stages.title: Graph invariants and the global ε, φ and Noether divisors
stages.description:
**Targets.** Zhang's invariants of polarized metrized graphs (ε, φ, τ, δ) and their inequalities (Cinkir, Baker–Rumely, de Jong), the local φ-invariant of a curve over a complete field, the global adelic divisors E_S and Φ_S that globalize ε and φ over a base, the triple-pairing identity for Φ_S, the boundary bounds (2g − 2)Δ_S ≥ E_S and Φ_S ≥ Δ_S/39, the Hodge lower decomposition of ⟨ω_a, ω_a⟩, the Gross–Schoen height variation, Faltings' δ-invariant, the arithmetic Noether formula and the admissible Noether divisor Ξ_S.

**Sources.** Yuan §§3.2–3.4, 4.5.2, pp. 46–55 and 89–91; Zhang 2010; Cinkir 2011; Baker–Rumely 2007; de Jong 2018; Wilms 2017.

stages.title: Bigness of the admissible canonical bundle
stages.description:
**Targets.** The uniform positive lower bound for φ on compact Riemann surfaces of genus g, bigness of ⟨ω_a, ω_a⟩ in the geometric and arithmetic cases (Theorem 3.2), and the main theorem: ω_{X/S,a} is nef and big under maximal variation (Theorems 1.3/3.1).

**Sources.** Yuan §§3.4–3.5 and §3.1, pp. 40, 55–59.

stages.title: Potential bigness
stages.description:
**Targets.** Potential bigness of a nef adelic line bundle on a family with geometrically integral generic fibre, integrality of relative powers, the mixed intersection and Deligne-pairing coefficient computations on relative powers, Theorem 4.1 (bigness of π_*⟨L^{e+1}⟩ ⟺ potential bigness), the product-grid degree bound, Theorem 4.5 for the Abel, difference and universal-shift families, and cross-characteristic restriction.

**Sources.** Yuan §§4.1–4.2, pp. 59–70, and p. 82.

stages.title: Admissible self-intersection and the Faltings height
stages.description:
**Targets.** The stable Faltings height over function fields, global graph invariants and Zhang's correction, lower bounds of ω_a² by φ, the function-field comparison (Theorem 4.11), Wilms' lower bound for δ, Bost's lower bound for the Faltings height (with the normalization corrected), the boundary-coercive divisor, the number-field comparison (Theorem 4.14) and the uniform comparison c₃max{h_Fal, 1} ≤ [ω_a²] ≤ c₄max{h_Fal, 1} (Theorem 1.4).

**Sources.** Yuan §4.3.1, §4.5, pp. 70–73 and 84–96; Wilms 2017, 2022; Looper–Silverman–Wilms.
